display.title: Learning Leads to Action: Never Lose Your Temper
display.summary_short: A short talk: Torah learning must turn into good deeds and good midos, starting with self-control, because the Sages compare anger to idol worship.
display.summary_long: A two-minute talk from the Tzivos Hashem radio show. Uncle Yossi teaches that although learning Torah is very important, what counts most is action: carrying what we learn into our lives through good character and kindness to others. Quoting the Mishnah that 'not study but action is the main thing', he singles out one of the Sages' most important rules, self-control: always be patient and never lose your temper. The Sages say that a person who becomes angry is like someone who worships idols. In the full broadcast this talk introduced a story about a man whose temper got him into serious trouble.
display.lesson: Turn your learning into action: be patient and never lose your temper.

date.note: Cut from episode 120 (Rosh Chodesh Nissan 5744); the same talk is also found in episodes 30 and 161.
